newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - April 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - April 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has shown concern over Westpac Banking Corp's A$1.44 billion takeover bid for the Bank of Melbourne. Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has also reacted to the bid, claiming the Government would not be pushed into overturning bank merger rules before the release of the Wallis report into the financial system. Page 1.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has released a report stating Pacific Rim economies will outstrip the rest of the world in terms of economic growth in 1997 and 1998. The report said growth in Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea will expand by 3.2 per cent in 1997 and 3.1 per cent in 1998. Page 4. --

Data released yesterday by the Australian Bureau of Statistics show job vacancies grew by 1.9 per cent in trend terms over the previous three months. The latest figures revealing a modest sign of recovery are at their highest level in trend terms since November 1994. Overtime date also released by the Bureau shows the amount of overtime worked was up 3.7 per cent in the three months to February. Page 4.

An imminent Industrial Relations Court decision on whether workers at a Tasmanian potato processing plant were unfairly dismissed could create a legal minefield to the growing practice of outsourcing workers. The Communications Electrical and Plumbing Unin claims Simplot Australia breached obligations to pay redundancy benefits and breached unfair dismissal laws when 12 workers were transferred to a labour hire company to provide services at the plant. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The proposed merger between Westpac Bank and the Bank of Melbourne has been put on hold until the Federal Government responds to an inquiry into the financial system. Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has ruled out approving Westpac's A$1.4 billion bid to buy the Victoria's biggest regional bank until Cabinet considers the findings of the soon to be released Wallis inquiry. Page 1.

Western Australia is in mourning today after the discovery of Ciara Glennon's body in bushland 40 kilometres north of Perth yesterday morning. Glennon was last seen outside a city hotel on March 14. Police now believe they are one step closer in capturingthe serial killer believed responsible for Glennon's death and the death of two other women over a 15 month period. Page 1.

The Federal Government has called an urgent meeting of the country's health officials in response to Victoria's worsening salmonella crisis in the meat industry. The call for the national summit comes a day after a routine check in Western Australia uncovered a salmonella strain in processed meat sourced from a Melbourne plant of Australia's largest smallgoods manufacturer, Don Smallgoods. Page 1.

A commission of inquiry investigating Sandline International's contract with the Papua New Guinea Government has heard the mercenary group offered to provide their services at a discount to the PNG Government in return for a stake in the lucrative Bougainille copper mine and suggested Australian-based mining group RTZ-CRA might subsidise the deal. The evidence was contained in a letter written by Sandline chief executive, Lieutenant-Colonel Tim Spicer late last year. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

An efficiency report to be taken to Cabinet next week by Defence Minister Ian McLachlan recommends that up to 8000 military and civilian jobs be cut as part of a major revamp to Australia's defence force. Government sources say McLachlan supports the findngs, which advocates a shift in spending from personnel to military hardware. Page 1

The University of Sydney plans to offer extra university places to several hundred students for a cost of up to A$100,000 for a four-year degree. A discussion plan prepared by the University vice-chancellor Professor Gavin Brown suggests the places be offred only in specific high demand courses such as law and veterinary science. Page 1.

After a marathon nine-day hearing, the New South Wales Industrial Commission yesterday ruled Kim Hollingsworth was unfairly dismissed from her job as a trainee police officer two years ago because police claimed she lied in her trainee application form whn she failed to mention she had previously worked as a prostitute and stripper. Page 1.

A key member of New South Wales' top education board, Dame Leonie Kramer, six years ago approved two texts for school study lists without reading them and now, in a reversal of her decision, wants the books banned from the State's classrooms. Kramer confimed she approved Top Girls, by Caryl Churchill, and the novel Fineflour, by Gillian Mears despite being officially alerted the books could cause community alarm. Page 3.
THE AGE

The Federal Government has warned Westpac not to expect automatic approval of its bid to merge with the Bank of Melbourne following concerns about reduced competition within the banking sector and the potential loss of up to 1500 jobs. Westpac yesterday lanched a A$1.44 billion bid for Victoria's biggest regional bank. Page 1.

The Victorian Opposition is considering a Supreme Court action to force a Liberal MP Bruce Atkinson to quit his seat following the confirmation he worked on 15 private projects for local government while a member of Parliament. The Labor party assert Atkison had breach the State's Constitution Act which prevents MPs having commercial dealings with the Crown. Page 1.

Former Coles Myer chief executive Brian Quinn denied defrauding the retail giant over renovations to the values of A$4.46 million to his former home. Presenting evidence for the first time in the current trial against him, Quinn told the court he had neve been involved in a conspiracy with a former Coles Myer national maintenance manager to do anything dishonest on his behalf. Page 1.

Independent Senator Mal Colston, under attack for allegedly abusing parliamentary travel allowances which have amounted to A$136,000 over five years, has withdrawn his claim for a pay rise without comment. The Queensland Senator came under fire from the Oposition following yesterday's revelations that a pay increase application had been made. Page A3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
